Gaussian elimination: delivery audit

Instructional inventory

The review draft contains a full derivation of equation equivalence, exact rectangular elimination, a termination invariant, generalized substitution, complete affine solution families, a canonical RREF proof, left-null impossibility witnesses, parameter branches, LU and permuted LU, square and rectangular inverses, scalar work counts, declared rounding, residual amplification and finite-field contrasts.

The finite bank contains 71 fully solved tasks: two authentic examination items, including one explicit master's revisit, and 69 original/course-derived mathematical and conceptual tasks. Twelve complete elimination problems display every nontrivial row operation plus particular, homogeneous and transform certificates. The remaining tasks include proofs, medium/hard parameter families, algorithm defects, LU normalization and later-swap traps, arithmetic-field comparisons and constrained solution extensions. The end-of-chapter summary is followed by 80 complete examination rules.

Mathematical checks

Exact fraction certificates independently check each complete-reduction input, every displayed reduced array, every particular solution and null direction. Each serialized rational elimination checkpoint is checked against its original array and invertible transform. LU and PLU checkpoints are checked by exact multiplication. Exceptional parameter classifications are checked directly before division. Finite-field solutions are exhaustively substituted in their declared field. Decimal rounding and small-residual examples use explicitly named models.

The dedicated verifier also validates the authentic LU column and scaled factorization, the coupled integer count, determinant-ratio and work-count formulas, coordinate maps, inverse products and a family of independently generated rectangular systems. These checks are reproducible finite evidence and are not represented as proofs of universal numerical accuracy.

Diagrams, simulations and typography

Seven original SVG teaching figures show equation geometry, transformation certificates, nonconsecutive pivot columns, affine directions, contradiction witnesses, parameter branches and stored-multiplier swaps. Twelve original animated models show actual matrix-value changes, persistent row movement or geometric coordinate movement. Every simulation includes a declared invariant/model, exact checkpoint explanations, pause/play, previous/next, reset, seek, speed and enlargement.

The rational laboratory accepts integer/fraction input with bounded dimensions, stores exact row-operation matrices and reports a unique solution, affine family or contradiction. It rejects malformed fractions and ragged matrices. It does not use a numerical tolerance or claim to implement arbitrary finite fields.

Mathematics uses native MathML with STIX Two Math, including matrix tables, fractions, indices and summation limits. Prose and headings retain the approved Source Sans 3 and Newsreader families. Code uses JetBrains Mono. References are fully English and links have no underline.

Desktop, 390-pixel mobile and print inspection cover formulas, SVG labels, question solutions and laboratory controls. The final evidence files identify the actual checked cases and any corrected findings. Stored study progress and all 25 earlier approvals remain intact.

Boundaries and approval gate

The five-course candidate pool and inspected examination pages are finite and explicitly named. No claim is made to inspect all global courses, reproduce inaccessible homework, certify every browser or guarantee correct answers to every unseen examination question. Numerical sparse methods, QR/SVD and full rank-space theory have their own later scope.

This chapter remains a review draft. Explicit student approval is required before promotion and before starting the next chapter. No next chapter is authored during this delivery.
